messages:
nina: Trying to wire up the terraform quickstart for a customer demo. First `generate` works, then the app hits a bunch of 401/402s and the process hangs because the client keeps retrying.

harry: which auth are you using in the terraform script? service account vs workspace API key?

nina: service_account: I provisioned a service account and set REDWOOD_SERVICE_KEY to the JSON path in the demo container.

harry: ok. quick sanity: run `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami` with the same creds. it will show workspace and billing_state.

nina: output: `{\"workspace_id\":\"w-demo-01\",\"billing_state\":\"unpaid\"}` so looks gated. Hadn't realized terraform-created workspace needs a billing link to be active.

harry: yep — onboarding nuance: service accounts use refresh tokens under the hood; the SDK used to retry on refresh 4xx which causes hangs in non-interactive runs like yours. two options: use a workspace-scoped API key for demos, or set the client to fail fast in CI/demo: `REDWOOD_CLIENT_RETRY_MAX=0`.

nina: switching to a workspace key fixed the hang and the demo completes. would be great if the quickstart terraform module printed a friendly message when a workspace is unpaid.

harry: agreed. we should add a post-provision step in the terraform quickstart that calls whoami and fails with an actionable message if billing_state != active. also add a note in the README about workspace billing for demo synths.

devex-bot: Created TASK-991: \"quickstart-terraform: detect unpaid workspace after provisioning and surface actionable error\" assigned to harry. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/TASK-991 :sparkles:

nina: thanks — will update our internal demo runbook after TASK-991 lands to prefer workspace API keys for ephemeral demos.
